title: The Single Divine Operation and Christ's Victory over Death
english: They come as partners, and concerning them a lot is cast. If someone leaves an only-begotten son and appoints him as successor, all the things belonging to the deceased are his, and no lot is cast. But when many come upon the true heir saying, 'We too are children of him,' a division of his garments occurs. But they are not divided, only the words; for the same word does not lie with the same mind differently according to heretics. Each one pulls the word toward his own mindset and will. Therefore, the diligent and truly faithful one possesses the whole robe of Jesus, not having it torn; so he does not cast a lot; the whole is his. For even if they cast a lot and use the words, they do not become his, they do not become masters of them; for a wise man according to Christ comes into the midst and shows that what he thinks is his is not his.

And what about garments and clothing? The garments together are called clothing, but each one by itself is not called clothing. And just as many sheep gathered together at once are called a flock, but each one is not called a flock, and people who have come together into one are called a people, but each one is not called a people. 20 'But You, Lord, do not delay Your help' (Psalm 70:5). If they exerted themselves in these things, even if they bring tribulation upon me, I have entreated You not to turn away, 'for tribulation is near' (Psalm 70:6). And the tribulation, if it has become near from those surrounding me like calves and bulls, from those scattering my bones, from those becoming causes to me such that my tongue is stuck to my throat, but You, do not delay Your help. Immediately then the resurrection of the Savior occurred, and immediately those who were scandalized turned back to Him. So the help has not been far.

And these things, according to the intention of man, Jesus says: 'Do not delay Your help.' The help which is required happens from no one else but from God. And I said that, when 'God' is said, it does not always signify the Father, separating the Son, nor the Son dividing from the Father; for the divinity is one. And because it is thus, we call the help the resurrection from the dead. Where it is said that He has delivered Himself and has been raised, and where the Father is said to be...

He has given [life] and has raised [him], from which it is shown that the one resurrection and the one work being done by Father and Son happens through only one divine energy. Even if the Father does [it], as God working this, he works it; even if the Son, he does this as God.

20 Pay attention to my understanding. For if you pay attention to my understanding, the help is not far from me, but being near, it worked; for he says previously these things concerning the men: for he did not come so that previously he himself might die and rise, but through others. 'By the grace of God he was raised above all death' (Rom 6:9). All died on behalf of them. This one by the grace of God was raised above all. 'The love of God holds us together, judging this thing to be that if one died on behalf of all, then all died' (Rom 6:10), so that those having died might no longer be dead, 'but live by that one who died on behalf of them and rose' (Rom 6:10). Some human power is able to give [life] on behalf of another, and some reproach is able to be received on behalf of another, and a rebuke. But death, no one is able to receive on behalf of another. And behold: he was raised alone, he was not swallowed by it, nor did it consume him. But he who is being swallowed by death swallows it himself. 'Death, having prevailed, swallowed [up]' (1 Cor 15:55). This one swallowed death, the one having been laid under it. And since Jesus 'did not commit sin,' and through the seizing of sin death is swallowed and swallows the one sinning—therefore he was raised above all; indeed, he was raised. And he has given the reason: 'so that through death he might render powerless the one having the power of death' (Heb 2:14). In death he destroyed death.

28 Save my soul from the sword (Ps 54:23). Jesus is also the one saying this verse, and he is able to say this also concerning his own soul, which he had the power to cast out and take back, and concerning every soul made his own. Just as it is said each of the saints is not merely a man anymore, but a man of God, so a soul desiring to please God is not merely a soul anymore, but a soul of God. Thus, in either way, he says these things concerning his own soul and that which he received, and concerning every soul made his own. And the sword sometimes signifies punishment; as if it is said: 'in the sword all sinful people of the people shall perish'; for it has never happened in history.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Sword and the Unity of the Person
english: So that the whole people might be cut down by the sword. Some of them died, but not all. He says this: all sinners will be tested by execution. He sometimes reveals both an evil power and the devil himself; for when it is said regarding Mary, 'and a sword will pierce your own soul' (Luke 2:35), he speaks of the adversary. When he casts thoughts upon someone or wishes to cast them, if that soul does not receive them, they pass through it, like the fifth arrow of the Psalm (Ps 42:5) when it is sent not at the mark, passing through the archer.

He cast [it] into Judas; he acted against Judas. He did not secure himself, he did not guard against it: 'do not give place to the devil' (Eph 5:11), and he did not pass it by; for it entered into him. And he who says, 'I did not know the evil one passing away from me,' had the sword passing through. To not know here does not mean ignorance, but not having been tested. Thus, even those who despise to say something, even if it is present, even if it is, say: 'I do not know.'

Regarding 'save': the 'save' certainly means all this: 'save me, having seized me and being under it.' Save me so that I may not suffer anything from it. Regarding: who is speaking? They wish to say this: 'if he speaks about the soul himself, who is the one speaking? It is a body that is speaking.' But those saying such things stumble.

In composite things, each of those in the composition is said of the whole composition. 'Your whole spirit and soul and body.' Is the spirit something else from the men, and the soul something else, and the body? Therefore they posit [them as separate]. We often speak about a city, saying it has a bad city, a bad ruler, a bad people, bad laws, not right ones. What is the city apart from the bad rulers, the counselors, and the people? And just as we speak about the human body, saying a head of the body, a face of the body, a hand of the body, feet—is the body something other than these, while each is something else beside itself? Those who have done the logical things well understand these things easily. See: everything having sensation and soul is an animal, and I say that the animal is not a man, nor a horse, nor an ox. But I say this: that man is not the whole genus, nor is he the whole animal. And I say each...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Humiliation and Exaltation of the People and the Son
english: He has souls; but this one he has as unique, for it is unshakeable. And I say unshakeable in this way: not being turned; for that which is called unshakeable in a completed sense signifies the unchangeable. When I say that the righteous man is not turned toward injustice, I say the righteous is unshakeable in the measure that he possesses righteousness; for the unshakeable does not turn. But not everything that does not turn is unshakeable.

Therefore, this soul is unique to him among the others, because it alone possesses the capacity to be always with him. No reasoning, no impulse, no disturbance can separate it; for even if it is disturbed, the disturbance stands only as a pre-passion. For this was shown through the 'now', seeing that the 'now' does not signify continuous time, but the significant moment, the non-existent time. All time has three divisions, but this 'now' has none, for it is the boundary of time.

"He began to be terrified and to be in anguish" (Ps 22:16). Until the beginning, one cannot receive a pre-passion instead of cowardice; for pre-passion is a testing of nature, not making a quality bad or serious, unless it takes on the following things so that it is no longer a pre-passion. Often these things have been distinguished for us as being four: pre-passion alone releases an inclination, it does not subject one to an inclination; but passion is with a moderate inclination; and the disposition is then malice; and much more is the action once taken up.

"Save me from the mouth of the lion" (Ps 22:20). Here he can also call the devil a "lion", for he attacked in the time of the passion. Indeed, when it was said in the forty-day temptation that "the devil departed from him", it is adjacent in the Gospel to "until a time" (Lk 22:36). Then again, it came when the passion was. And since I was saying that the attacks are brought to the man of the Savior himself and to his own, when Peter says or the Savior says to Peter, "Behold, Satan has demanded you" (Lk 22:31), in a way he wanted to devour the members of the Savior by attacking against the Savior. He says, therefore, "Save me from the mouth of the lion". He can also call that people a "lion", for "it became [said] my heritage is to me like a lion in the thicket" (Ps 22:10). May I not suffer these things which they want to dispose me toward. He says these things because every rational essence, even if it is perfect, needs the alliance from God. "Save me from the mouth of the lion."

And 'from the horns of the unicorns my humiliation' he can say here, referring to the multitude of the Jews, the people of Israel; for he said in Jeremiah: 'I have forsaken my house, I have left my inheritance. My inheritance became to me like a lion in a forest' (Jeremiah 12:7). Having been a people whom I placed in Paradise, where there was much fruit, when they had turned into wildness, then consequently they nest in fruitless trees—for the forest is nothing other than a place of fruitless trees. Therefore, they encamp there. And my inheritance, which I had so that it might be a people and a portion of the Lord, was so provoked against me as to be thrown upon a lion, not a lion being tamed—for often lions come into human places being tamed—but as in a forest, as a wild beast.

And it can also be said concerning the devil; for we say this also, that after the temptation in the wilderness it is said: 'He has departed for a time.' 'And from the horns of the unicorns my humiliation' (Psalm 92:10). The unicorn is a strong animal. It is not subject to man, it is not tamed by man. 'From the horns' therefore, 'the humiliation of the unicorns,' the cross and death saying his own humiliation. 'He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even the death of the cross' (Philippians 2:8). My humiliation, therefore, then, flows from these unicorns—and these are also some evil enemies—then, when I rise from the dead; for 'the kings of the earth and the rulers were gathered together' to surround him with death. Then God delivers him from his humiliation; he rises from the dead. And all these things are spoken concerning the man.

Therefore, without delay he immediately brought forward: 'I will declare your name to my brothers' (Acts 13:34). 'I will proclaim your name to my brothers; and again: behold, I will be trusting in him, behold, I and the children whom God has given to me.' And again: 'Wherefore he ought to have been made like his brothers in all things' (Hebrews 2:17). Not only according to the body, but according to all things. According to his divinity, the only-begotten Son of God does not have a brother; for if he had a brother, he would not be only-begotten. But to have brothers is opposed to being an only-begotten one. The only-begotten has no brothers. The one having brothers is not only-begotten.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
